title: Constitution and Government
lines: USAT asks how Pakistan's constitutions developed and how the state is organised under the 1973 Constitution: the houses of Parliament, the President and Prime Minister, the courts and the constitutional bodies. Questions use stable facts. They do not ask who holds office today, and numbers of seats change by amendment, so learn the structure rather than seat counts.
## Road to a constitution
- Until 1956 Pakistan was governed under the Government of India Act 1935, adapted, with the Governor-General as head of state.

- The Objectives Resolution was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by the first Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949. It declared that sovereignty belongs to Allah, exercised by the people within limits He has set, and promised democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance, social justice and protection of minorities. It became the preamble of later constitutions and, in 1985, a substantive part of the 1973 Constitution.
- The first Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1954. The One Unit scheme (1955) merged the provinces of West Pakistan into one province.
## Three constitutions compared
| Enforced | 23 March 1956 | 8 June 1962 | 14 August 1973
| System | parliamentary | presidential | federal parliamentary
| Legislature | one house | one house | two houses: National Assembly and Senate
| Election of President | by assemblies | through Basic Democracies (indirect) | electoral college of both houses and provincial assemblies
| Ended | martial law, October 1958 | abrogated, March 1969 | in force (with amendments)
- The 1956 Constitution named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and was based on parity between East and West Pakistan. Iskander Mirza became the first President.
- The 1962 Constitution was given by Ayub Khan and made the President powerful. The first general elections on adult franchise came later, in December 1970.

- The 1973 Constitution was passed by the National Assembly on 10 April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973. It was framed by an assembly elected on adult franchise and was agreed by all the major parties.
## Structure under the 1973 Constitution
| Body | Key facts
| Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) | the President, the National Assembly and the Senate
| National Assembly | elected directly; term five years unless dissolved earlier; presided over by the Speaker; elects the Prime Minister
| Senate | equal representation of the provinces; members serve six years, half retiring every three years; never dissolved; presided over by the Chairman
| President | head of state; term five years; must be a Muslim of at least 45; Chairman of the Senate acts in his absence
| Prime Minister | head of government; leads the federal cabinet, which answers to the National Assembly
| Governor | appointed by the President for each province
| Chief Minister | head of a provincial government, elected by the provincial assembly
## Courts and constitutional bodies
- Supreme Court: highest court; High Courts in each province and Islamabad.
- Federal Shariat Court (1980): examines whether laws are repugnant to the injunctions of Islam.
- Council of Islamic Ideology: advises Parliament on bringing laws in line with Islam.
- Council of Common Interests: settles federal-provincial policy matters. National Finance Commission: shares federal revenue among provinces.
- Election Commission of Pakistan: conducts elections.
## Articles worth knowing
| Article | Subject
| 2 | Islam is the state religion
| 6 | high treason
| 8 | laws inconsistent with fundamental rights are void
| 25 | equality of citizens
| 251 | Urdu is the national language
> Which feature belongs only to the 1973 Constitution?  (A) parliamentary system  (B) Islamic Republic as the name  (C) a two-house Parliament  (D) indirect election through Basic Democracies
> C. The 1956 Constitution was also parliamentary and used the name Islamic Republic; Basic Democracies belonged to 1962. Only 1973 created the Senate.

> A bill passed by the National Assembly is rejected by the Senate. Under the Constitution it may be referred to  (A) the Supreme Court  (B) a joint sitting of Parliament  (C) the President alone  (D) a referendum
> B. Disagreement between the houses is resolved in a joint sitting.
## Traps
! The Objectives Resolution was passed in 1949 but the first constitution only in 1956.
! The Senate is the house of equal provincial representation; the National Assembly seats follow population.
! The 18th Amendment (2010) increased provincial autonomy and renamed NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
## Quick check
- Constitutions: 1956 parliamentary, 1962 presidential, 1973 federal parliamentary.
- 1973: passed 10 April, enforced 14 August; two houses.
- NA five years; Senate six-year terms, half every three; President at least 45.
